page.layout: One page of text: the title block at the head, then one column of verse with an initial woodcut. Page number top left. Catchword "Hæc" at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: GEORGII BVCHANANI SCOTI, DE SPHÆRA LIB. IIII.
main_text.p: NVne mihi stellarúmque ortus obitúsque canenti
main_text.l: Sis facilis, causas penitus dum promo la-
tenies,
Cur lenta Oceanum fugiant hæc, illa repente
Signa per obliquum properent ascendere cœlum:
Cur iterum salsas subeant hæc ocyus undas,
Illa trahant tardos lento molimine gressus.
Cur ubi Sol mediam cœli conscendit in arcem,
Longior hic, alibi contractior exeat umbra,
Cur Phœbea suas consumat pyramis umbras,
Cur hic æqua dies semper cum nocte recurrat,
Una dies, & nox una illic finiat annum:
Qualiter e gremio magna telluris in oras,
Luminis herba recens tenerum cum tollit acumen,
Et cœlo se se offendit, tum dicimus ortum,
Aut quibus indulsit melior natura moveniem
Membra animam, lucem cum primum hauserè parētis,
Mox egressa aluo, nata atque exorta putamus:
At cum fracta malis aut fessa senilibus annis
In gremium terræ recidunt, sese que resoluunt,
Exinguïnque oculos, occasum obitúmque vocamus.

page.notes: The initial N is a decorated woodcut letter, read as N joined to "Vne". Line 3 "tenies," and line 16 "moveniem" are doubtful and read as printed. The running head at the top is too faint to read and is left out. Faint marks in the right margin are not text.
